AAOI.short: Optical transceivers that carry data as light inside data centres.
AAOI.operations: Designs and makes fibre-optic networking parts, with operations in the United States, Taiwan and China.
AAOI.mission: Aims to supply the light-based parts that move data inside data centres and across cable and phone networks.

AAPL.short: iPhone, Mac and services — the world's biggest consumer technology company.
AAPL.operations: Sells phones, computers, tablets, watches and headphones worldwide, and runs online stores and paid services such as music, television and payments.
AAPL.mission: To design, make and market its own devices and services for shoppers, small businesses, schools, companies and governments around the world.

ADBE.short: Photoshop and the creative software suite, now adding AI design tools.
ADBE.operations: Operates worldwide, selling content creation tools to individuals, teams and large companies, plus marketing, publishing and advertising services for brands.
ADBE.mission: To give individuals, teams and businesses the tools to create, publish and promote content.

AEHR.short: Burn-in machines that stress-test chips, both on the wafer and after packaging.
AEHR.operations: Supplies chip testing machines and related parts to chipmakers and testing firms in the United States, Asia, Europe and the Middle East.
AEHR.mission: To provide systems that test and stress semiconductor devices before shipment, at wafer, single-chip and packaged stages.

AFRM.short: Affirm — buy-now-pay-later lending offered at online checkouts.
AFRM.operations: Runs a payment service that lets shoppers pay in instalments at small shops, large chains, online brands and travel sites, with funding from partner banks and investors.
AFRM.mission: To let people spread the cost of a purchase over time through a payment network shared with the shops they buy from.

AIRJ.short: Early-stage technology that pulls water from air to cool and dehumidify data centres.
AIRJ.operations: Very small firm with technology that pulls water out of the air, plus dehumidifying, cooling, heat pump and water-recovery systems, including for data centres.
AIRJ.mission: To capture drinking-quality water and useful energy from the moisture in ordinary air.

ALAB.short: Connectivity chips that link AI processors together at very high speed.
ALAB.operations: Small chip designer operating in the United States and Taiwan, selling to very large data-centre operators and equipment makers.
ALAB.mission: Aims to move data quickly between the parts inside cloud and artificial-intelligence computers.

AMAT.short: Equipment that deposits and etches the microscopic layers inside every chip.
AMAT.operations: Supplies chip factory equipment, services and software in the United States, China, Korea, Taiwan, Japan, Southeast Asia and Europe, through two business arms.
AMAT.mission: To provide the equipment, services and know-how that chipmakers use to build semiconductors.

AMD.short: Designs computer processors and AI chips — Nvidia's main challenger.
AMD.operations: Designs chips sold internationally through three business lines: data centres, personal computers and gaming, and equipment with chips built in.
AMD.mission: To supply processors, graphics chips and artificial-intelligence hardware for business and consumer computing worldwide.

AMKR.short: Packages and tests finished chips on behalf of other chip companies.
AMKR.operations: Packages and tests finished chips for other companies, with operations in the United States, Japan, Europe and the Asia-Pacific region.
AMKR.mission: To handle the final packaging and testing steps for chipmakers, device makers and factories that do not do this work themselves.

AMPX.short: High-energy silicon-anode batteries for drones and aviation.
AMPX.operations: Develops and makes lithium-ion batteries at its base in Fremont, California, sold mainly to makers of drones and other unmanned aircraft.
AMPX.mission: To supply batteries built for aviation uses, especially drones and high-flying unmanned craft that stay aloft for long periods.

AMZN.short: Online shopping giant, and the world's largest cloud-computing provider (AWS).
AMZN.operations: Runs online and physical shops in North America and other countries, plus a large computing-rental arm and its own devices such as Kindle and Echo.
AMZN.mission: To sell consumer goods, advertising and subscriptions through online and physical stores in North America and internationally.

ANET.short: High-speed network switches that connect the servers in AI data centres.
ANET.operations: Sells computer-network equipment and software across the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific, direct and through resellers.
ANET.mission: Aims to supply the networking gear that connects data centres, offices and cloud services.

APH.short: Connectors and cables — the physical plumbing of all electronics.
APH.operations: Three segments making electrical, electronic and fibre-optic connectors, cables and sensors in the United States, China and other countries.
APH.mission: Aims to supply the connectors and cables that join electronic equipment in cars, planes, phones and data centres.

APLD.short: Builds and rents out data centres designed for AI computing.
APLD.operations: Designs, builds and runs data centres in North America, hosting machines for crypto mining customers and renting computing power to artificial-intelligence developers.
APLD.mission: Aims to supply the buildings, electricity and computing capacity that artificial-intelligence and other heavy computing customers need.

APP.short: Advertising software that helps mobile apps and games find new users.
APP.operations: Two segments, advertising and apps, serving advertisers, mobile app publishers, small businesses and streaming TV companies in the US and abroad.
APP.mission: To provide advertising tools driven by artificial intelligence that help businesses find and reach customers.

ARM.short: Licenses the chip blueprints used inside nearly every smartphone in the world.
ARM.operations: Licenses chip blueprints rather than making chips, serving chipmakers, device makers and computing-rental firms for phones, cars and data centres.
ARM.mission: To research, develop and license chip designs, software and tools that other companies use to build their own chips.

ASML.short: The only company that makes the EUV machines needed for the most advanced chips.
ASML.operations: Sells, upgrades and services the machines that print circuit patterns onto chips, supporting chipmakers across Asia, Europe and North America.
ASML.mission: To provide the advanced printing, measuring and inspection machines that chipmakers need to produce semiconductors.

ASTS.short: Building satellites that connect directly to ordinary mobile phones from space.
ASTS.operations: Designs and develops its BlueBird satellites from a base in Midland, Texas, to carry a mobile phone network in space.
ASTS.mission: To run a mobile network from satellites so ordinary smartphones get service in places with no coverage on the ground.

AVAV.short: Military drones and loitering munitions for the US and allied forces.
AVAV.operations: Makes small pilotless aircraft, one-way strike drones, and space and cyber equipment for government agencies and businesses in the US and abroad.
AVAV.mission: To supply robotic aircraft and related defence technology that give military users useful information and precise firepower.

AVGO.short: Custom AI chips and networking parts, plus a large enterprise software business.
AVGO.operations: Supplies chips and business software internationally through two arms: semiconductor products and infrastructure software.
AVGO.mission: To design and supply the chips and software that run company networks, data centres, telephone systems and broadband.

AXON.short: Tasers, police body cameras, drones and the evidence software behind them.
AXON.operations: Sells public safety equipment and cloud software in the US and abroad, including TASER stun devices, body cameras and evidence-handling services.
AXON.mission: To equip police and other first responders with cameras, less-lethal devices and software for storing and sharing video evidence.

AXTI.short: Grows the crystal wafers (indium phosphide) that optical components are built on.
AXTI.operations: Makes the wafer discs chips are built on, selling directly in the US, China and Europe and via agents in Japan, Taiwan and Korea.
AXTI.mission: Aims to supply specialty base materials used in lasers, sensors, wireless devices and solar cells.

BE.short: Bloom Energy — fuel cells that generate on-site electricity for data centres.
BE.operations: Designs and builds fuel-cell units that turn natural gas, biogas or hydrogen into on-site electricity for data centres, utilities, hospitals, schools, shops and factories.
BE.mission: To supply clean, reliable electricity generated right where it is used, without burning the fuel.

BKNG.short: Booking.com, Priceline and Agoda — the world's biggest online travel agency.
BKNG.operations: Runs travel and restaurant booking websites including Booking.com, Priceline, Agoda, KAYAK and OpenTable, used by travellers and hotel owners worldwide.
BKNG.mission: To help people book somewhere to stay, a way to get there and a table to eat at, all in one place online.

BWXT.short: Builds the nuclear reactors that power US Navy submarines and carriers.
BWXT.operations: Makes nuclear components and fuel, including precision parts for naval reactors, plus medical radioisotopes, steam generators and engineering services.
BWXT.mission: To supply nuclear parts, fuel and services to government and commercial customers and support power plants through their life.

CAT.short: Caterpillar — the world's biggest maker of construction and mining machinery.
CAT.operations: Makes diggers, loaders, mining trucks, engines, turbines and locomotives sold worldwide, and also lends customers the money to buy them.
CAT.mission: To supply the machines and engines used to build, mine and move things around the world.

CCJ.short: Cameco — one of the world's largest uranium miners.
CCJ.operations: Mines, mills and sells uranium and runs fuel refining and conversion, plus its Westinghouse arm which makes reactor equipment; sells in the Americas, Europe and Asia.
CCJ.mission: To supply uranium and nuclear fuel services used to generate electricity around the world.

CDNS.short: The software that engineers use to design computer chips.
CDNS.operations: Sells software, testing hardware and ready-made circuit designs to electronics and chip makers, and works in partnership with NVIDIA.
CDNS.mission: To provide the software, hardware and design building blocks that engineers use to design computer chips and electronic systems.

CEG.short: America's largest nuclear power operator, selling electricity to data centres.
CEG.operations: Runs about 31,676 megawatts of nuclear, wind, solar, natural gas and hydro power plants across the Mid-Atlantic, Midwest, New York and Texas.
CEG.mission: To produce and sell electricity, natural gas and cleaner energy services to homes, businesses and public bodies in the United States.

CGNX.short: Machine-vision systems that let factory robots and machines 'see'.
CGNX.operations: Sells camera-and-software systems that inspect goods on factory and warehouse lines, serving the United States, Europe and Greater China.
CGNX.mission: To automate factory and shipping work by letting machines see, identify, inspect and measure items such as phone parts and parcels.

CIFR.short: Bitcoin miner converting its power sites into AI data-centre hosting.
CIFR.operations: Builds and runs large data centres in the United States: one site currently powers bitcoin mining, with further sites being developed for big cloud-computing tenants.
CIFR.mission: Aims to develop industrial-scale data centres for bitcoin mining and for renting heavy computing capacity to large technology customers.

COHR.short: Lasers and optical components for data centres and industrial use.
COHR.operations: Three segments - networking, materials and lasers - making optical parts and laser systems for industry, communications and electronics worldwide.
COHR.mission: Aims to supply the light-based parts and laser machines used in factories, data centres and research.

CORZ.short: Former bitcoin miner now hosting AI and high-performance computing.
CORZ.operations: Runs data centres across the United States providing space, power, cooling and security to customers, and also operates its own machines that mine bitcoin.
CORZ.mission: Aims to supply the physical setting and power for heavy computing work, including artificial intelligence, alongside its digital-asset mining.

CRDO.short: High-speed cables and chips that move data inside AI server racks.
CRDO.operations: Sells high-speed cables, optical modules and chips in the United States, Taiwan, mainland China and Hong Kong, and licenses its designs.
CRDO.mission: Aims to move data quickly and reliably between machines in data centres.

CRM.short: Salesforce — the customer-management software used by sales teams worldwide.
CRM.operations: Sells customer-management software in the United States, Europe and Asia-Pacific to banks, hospitals, manufacturers, carmakers and government bodies.
CRM.mission: To connect companies with their customers through software, increasingly using automated assistants that work alongside staff.

CRSP.short: Gene-editing biotech; co-developed Casgevy, the first approved CRISPR medicine.
CRSP.operations: A Swiss-based gene-editing research company whose approved product Casgevy treats inherited blood disorders; it works closely with Vertex Pharmaceuticals.
CRSP.mission: Aims to develop gene-based medicines for serious illnesses, including blood disorders, cancer and type 1 diabetes.

CRWD.short: CrowdStrike — cloud security that protects company laptops and servers.
CRWD.operations: Sells computer security by subscription over the internet in the United States and internationally, protecting company devices, cloud systems and data.
CRWD.mission: To protect an organisation's devices, cloud systems, staff identities and data through one subscription platform.

CRWV.short: CoreWeave — rents Nvidia GPU computing power to AI companies.
CRWV.operations: Rents computing power over the internet in the United States, supplying specialist chips, storage and networking used for artificial-intelligence work.
CRWV.mission: Aims to run complex artificial-intelligence computing at large scale through its own cloud software and services.

DDOG.short: Monitoring software that tells companies the moment their systems break.
DDOG.operations: Runs an internet-based service that watches over customers' software and computer systems, sold in the United States and internationally.
DDOG.mission: To let organisations see how their software and computer systems are performing and keep them secure.

DE.short: Deere (John Deere) — the world's largest maker of farm machinery.
DE.operations: Makes tractors, harvesters, lawn equipment and construction and forestry machines sold worldwide, with a finance arm that lends buyers the money.
DE.mission: To make the machinery that farmers, builders and foresters rely on, with technology that makes their work more precise.

DELL.short: Servers and PCs; one of the largest suppliers of AI server systems.
DELL.operations: Designs, makes and sells computers and data-centre equipment across the Americas, Europe, the Middle East and Asia, split between business infrastructure and personal computers.
DELL.mission: Aims to supply computing products, services and financing to businesses, governments, schools, hospitals and consumers worldwide.

ENPH.short: Solar microinverters and home battery systems for rooftop solar.
ENPH.operations: Designs and sells home solar equipment in the United States and abroad, including small power converters, home batteries, monitoring software and car chargers.
ENPH.mission: To provide complete home energy systems built around rooftop solar, so households can make, store and manage their own electricity.

EOSE.short: Zinc-based batteries designed for long-duration electricity grid storage.
EOSE.operations: Makes large battery storage systems in the United States for power utilities, small local grids, and business and industrial customers.
EOSE.mission: To supply electricity storage that helps power grids handle growing complexity and swings in the price of power.

ETN.short: Eaton — electrical equipment that manages power in buildings and data centres.
ETN.operations: Makes electrical, aerospace, vehicle and hydraulic equipment through five divisions, selling in the US, Canada, Latin America, Europe and the Asia Pacific.
ETN.mission: To manage electrical and mechanical power for industrial, commercial and transport customers worldwide.

FLNC.short: Fluence — large grid-scale battery storage systems.
FLNC.operations: Builds large battery storage systems and the software that runs them, selling to power producers, utilities, developers and businesses in many countries.
FLNC.mission: To help electricity grids store power from wind and sun so it can be used when it is actually needed.

FN.short: Contract manufacturer that builds optical modules for other companies.
FN.operations: Contract manufacturer serving North America, Asia-Pacific and Europe, assembling optical and precision electronic products for other brands.
FN.mission: Aims to build complex optical and electronic products for the companies that design them.

FSLR.short: The largest US solar-panel maker, and a winner from tariffs on foreign solar.
FSLR.operations: Manufactures and sells solar panels and solar power solutions in the United States, France, India, Chile and other countries.
FSLR.mission: To supply solar panels made with its own thin-film technology, rather than the usual silicon, to utilities and large power projects.

FTNT.short: Fortinet — firewalls and network security hardware and software.
FTNT.operations: Sells computer security and networking products worldwide, including firewalls, its own security chips, and cloud-based protection services.
FTNT.mission: To bring computer networking and security together into one connected system for customers worldwide.

GE.short: GE Aerospace — builds and services jet engines for airlines and the military.
GE.operations: Designs, builds and services jet engines, propellers and aircraft systems for airlines and armed forces in North America, Europe, Asia and the Middle East.
GE.mission: To keep aircraft flying by making and maintaining the engines that power passenger and military planes.

GEV.short: GE Vernova — gas and wind turbines plus electricity grid equipment.
GEV.operations: Three divisions: Power (gas, nuclear, hydro, steam), Wind (onshore and offshore turbines) and Electrification (grid gear, solar, storage), selling in the US, Europe, Asia and Africa.
GEV.mission: To supply the equipment and services that generate, move, convert and store electricity.

GLW.short: Corning — optical fibre for networks and the tough glass on phone screens.
GLW.operations: Five businesses - optical cable, display glass, specialty materials, car parts and lab products - operating across the US, Asia and Europe.
GLW.mission: Aims to use its glass and ceramics know-how to serve communications, screens, cars and laboratories.

GOOGL.short: Google search and YouTube advertising, plus Google Cloud and Waymo self-driving cars.
GOOGL.operations: Runs search, advertising, phone software, video and email services across the Americas, Europe, Africa, the Middle East and Asia, plus a computing-rental arm.
GOOGL.mission: To offer a wide range of internet products and platforms, grouped into its main services, its computing-rental business and smaller ventures.

HNGE.short: Hinge Health — app-based physical therapy for back and joint pain.
HNGE.operations: Provides remote treatment for muscle, bone and joint problems, mainly to employers that pay their own staff health costs, using motion tracking and a wearable device.
HNGE.mission: Aims to build a health system that automates and widens care for back, muscle and joint pain, from injury through to recovery after surgery.

HOOD.short: Robinhood — the commission-free app for trading shares and crypto.
HOOD.operations: Runs an online investing service in the United States for shares and funds, and also offers credit cards, cash accounts and crypto wallets.
HOOD.mission: To let ordinary people invest easily in shares and funds, with free learning material alongside.

HPE.short: Enterprise servers, storage and networking equipment for data centres.
HPE.operations: Makes servers, storage and networking equipment and sells cloud and financing services worldwide, organised into five divisions.
HPE.mission: Aims to provide businesses around the world with the computing, storage and network equipment and services they rely on.

HUBB.short: Hubbell — electrical grid components and utility hardware.
HUBB.operations: Two divisions make power grid transmission and distribution components and communications gear, plus wiring devices, connectors and industrial controls, sold in the US and abroad.
HUBB.mission: To make and sell the electrical parts that power grids, buildings and industry depend on.

HUT.short: Owns power sites and data centres leased for AI; bitcoin mining held via a stake.
HUT.operations: Operates power and data-centre sites across the United States and Canada, used for bitcoin mining, data-centre services and renting computing power.
HUT.mission: Aims to combine electricity supply, data centres and computing capacity to serve customers whose work uses very large amounts of power.

HYLN.short: Hyliion — KARNO fuel-flexible generators; barely any revenue yet.
HYLN.operations: Small firm developing the KARNO power generator for fixed and mobile use, able to run on natural gas, propane, hydrogen or ammonia.
HYLN.mission: To build an electricity generator that can run on many different fuels, for both stationary and mobile use.

IBM.short: Enterprise software and consulting, plus one of the leading quantum computing programmes.
IBM.operations: Four segments - software, consulting, computing equipment and customer financing - with customers across the Americas, Europe, Africa, the Middle East and Asia.
IBM.mission: To provide combined computing products and services, centred on cloud computing and artificial intelligence, to large organisations.

INTC.short: The historic US chipmaker, now rebuilding both its chip designs and its factories.
INTC.operations: Designs and manufactures chips, with operations in the United States, Ireland and Israel, run as three units including a factory arm making chips for others.
INTC.mission: To design, make and sell computing products, and to build a manufacturing business that produces chips for other companies.

IONQ.short: Builds quantum computers using trapped ions; still early-stage and loss-making.
IONQ.operations: Builds quantum computers in the United States and Switzerland and sells access to them directly and through the Amazon, Microsoft and Google cloud services.
IONQ.mission: To develop quantum computers, plus quantum-based secure communications and detection systems, and sell access to and support for them.

IREN.short: Data-centre operator shifting from bitcoin mining to AI computing.
IREN.operations: Owns and runs data centres, electrical infrastructure and computing hardware in Australia and Canada, and mines bitcoin.
IREN.mission: Aims to own the whole chain behind its business, from electricity supply and buildings to the computers themselves.

ISRG.short: Maker of the da Vinci surgical robot used in hospitals worldwide.
ISRG.operations: Makes robotic surgery systems and instruments, sold with training and support to hospitals in the United States and internationally.
ISRG.mission: To widen access to surgery done through very small cuts, which is gentler on patients than traditional open operations.

JNJ.short: Johnson & Johnson — prescription medicines and medical devices.
JNJ.operations: Researches, makes and sells health products worldwide through two arms: prescription medicines, and medical devices for surgery, bones, the heart and eyes.
JNJ.mission: Aims to research, develop and sell medicines and medical devices for conditions such as cancer, immune disease, and heart and eye problems.

KEEL.short: Former crypto miner pivoting to AI data centres; still deeply loss-making.
KEEL.operations: Owns and runs data centres in the United States and Canada that house computers, and also provides electrical contracting work in Quebec.
KEEL.mission: To operate digital and energy sites in North America for heavy computing and artificial intelligence work.

KLAC.short: Inspection machines that find microscopic defects on chips during manufacturing.
KLAC.operations: Runs three business lines making inspection and measuring machines for chip and circuit-board plants, sold worldwide.
KLAC.mission: Aims to help chip makers find and fix flaws early so more of what they build works properly.

KO.short: Coca-Cola — the world's largest soft-drink company.
KO.operations: Makes drink concentrates and syrups sold worldwide through independent bottling partners, distributors and fountain retailers.
KO.mission: Aims to make and sell a wide range of non-alcoholic drinks, from soft drinks to water, coffee, tea and juice, around the world.

LEU.short: Centrus — the only US-owned uranium enricher, making HALEU fuel for new reactors.
LEU.operations: Supplies enriched uranium and other nuclear fuel components, and sells technical and manufacturing services, to customers in the US, Japan, the Netherlands and elsewhere.
LEU.mission: To supply the fuel that nuclear power plants run on, along with related technical and manufacturing work.

LITE.short: Lasers and optical modules; a key supplier for AI data-centre networking.
LITE.operations: Two segments, cloud and networking parts plus industrial lasers, selling across the Americas, Asia-Pacific, Europe, the Middle East and Africa.
LITE.mission: Aims to supply the light-based parts and lasers used in data centres, networks and factories.

LMND.short: Lemonade — app-based renters, home, car and pet insurance run largely by AI.
LMND.operations: Sells home, renters, landlord, car, pet and life insurance in the United States, Europe and the United Kingdom, and acts as agent for other insurers.
LMND.mission: To provide simple cover for stolen or damaged property and for accidents the customer is responsible for.

LMT.short: The world's largest defence contractor — F-35 fighter jets and missile defence.
LMT.operations: Four divisions - combat and transport aircraft, missiles, helicopters and space systems - selling mainly to the US government and to allied governments abroad.
LMT.mission: To research, design and build advanced defence and space technology for the United States government and its allies.

LRCX.short: Etching and deposition equipment, especially important for advanced memory chips.
LRCX.operations: Builds, services and refurbishes chip-making machines, selling into the United States, China, Korea, Taiwan, Japan, Southeast Asia and Europe.
LRCX.mission: Aims to supply the machines that lay down, carve and clean the layers used to build computer chips.

LUNR.short: Builds Moon landers plus satellites and space services for NASA and defence customers.
LUNR.operations: Builds Moon landers and provides delivery, data and support services from Houston, Texas, for NASA, defence bodies and commercial customers.
LUNR.mission: To carry cargo and equipment to the Moon and supply the communications and support services a working lunar economy would need.

LWLG.short: Pre-revenue developer of polymer materials that could speed up optical chips.
LWLG.operations: Very small development-stage firm in Colorado selling special light-controlling materials to chip foundries and optical module makers.
LWLG.mission: Aims to sell materials that let data move faster using light inside computer chips.

MA.short: Mastercard — operates one of the two big global card payment networks.
MA.operations: Processes card and account payments for banks, shops, businesses and governments in the United States and internationally.
MA.mission: To provide payment processing and related products and services worldwide as a technology company.

MCD.short: McDonald's — the world's largest fast-food restaurant chain.
MCD.operations: Owns, operates and franchises McDonald's restaurants in the United States and internationally, with most outlets run by franchisees.
MCD.mission: Aims to serve familiar fast food such as burgers, chicken, fries, breakfast and drinks through a largely franchised restaurant network.

MCHP.short: Microcontrollers and analog chips for cars, factory equipment and data centres.
MCHP.operations: Makes and sells small control chips across the Americas, Europe and Asia through two arms: semiconductor products and technology licensing.
MCHP.mission: To develop, make and sell smart, connected and secure control chips that sit inside other companies' equipment.

MDB.short: MongoDB — a widely used database for modern applications.
MDB.operations: Sells its database worldwide as a hosted online service, as software companies run themselves, and as a free version, plus consulting and training.
MDB.mission: To provide a general-purpose database that software developers use to store and organise information.

MELI.short: MercadoLibre — Latin America's Amazon, plus a large payments business.
MELI.operations: Runs online shopping sites in Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and beyond, with its own payments, lending, shipping and advertising arms.
MELI.mission: To make buying, selling, paying and borrowing online simple for people and small businesses across Latin America.

META.short: Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp — sells advertising to their billions of users.
META.operations: Runs Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger, plus a division making virtual-reality headsets and smart glasses, serving users in most world regions.
META.mission: To build products that let people connect and share with friends and family through phones, computers, headsets and smart glasses.

MMM.short: 3M — a diversified industrial: tapes, abrasives, safety gear and electronics.
MMM.operations: Makes abrasives, glues, safety gear, car and electronics materials and household goods, sold through shops, wholesalers, websites and direct sales.
MMM.mission: To apply its science to practical products for industry, transport, building, healthcare and the home.

MPWR.short: Power-management chips that feed clean, steady voltage to AI processors.
MPWR.operations: Designs power-management chips used in data centre servers, cars, appliances and networks, sold through distributors in China, Taiwan, Korea, Europe, the US and Japan.
MPWR.mission: To supply the semiconductor parts that convert and control electrical power inside electronic systems.

MRVL.short: Custom data-centre chips that move data between AI servers.
MRVL.operations: Designs data-centre and networking chips, with operations in the United States, Argentina, China, India, Israel, Japan, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan and Vietnam.
MRVL.mission: To supply the chips that move and store data from the heart of large data centres out to the edge of networks.

MSFT.short: Windows and Office software, Azure cloud computing, and a large stake in OpenAI.
MSFT.operations: Sells office and business software, rented computing power, Windows, game consoles and search advertising to people and companies worldwide.
MSFT.mission: To develop and support a broad set of technology products and services for individuals and businesses around the world.

MU.short: Memory chips, including the high-speed HBM memory that feeds AI processors.
MU.operations: Four business units making memory and storage chips, with sales in the US, Taiwan, Japan, mainland China, Hong Kong and Europe.
MU.mission: Aims to make the memory and storage chips used in data centres, phones, cars and computers.

MYRG.short: MYR Group — builds power lines, substations and data-centre electrical systems.
MYRG.operations: Builds and repairs power lines, substations and commercial wiring for utilities, contractors, building owners and governments in the US and Canada.
MYRG.mission: To build and maintain the electrical systems that carry power to homes, businesses and vehicles.

NBIS.short: Nebius — European AI cloud provider spun out of Yandex.
NBIS.operations: Builds and rents large banks of computers for artificial intelligence work in the US, UK and elsewhere; also owns a retraining school and a self-driving vehicle unit.
NBIS.mission: To build the full stack of computing infrastructure that the world's artificial intelligence industry needs.

NEE.short: NextEra — the largest US utility and the world's biggest wind and solar operator.
NEE.operations: Runs power plants using wind, sun, nuclear and natural gas plus power lines, batteries and pipelines; its Florida utility serves about 12 million people.
NEE.mission: To generate, store and deliver electricity across North America, leaning heavily on wind, sun and nuclear power.

NET.short: Cloudflare — speeds up and protects a large share of the world's websites.
NET.operations: Runs a worldwide network that protects and speeds up business websites, plus tools for software builders and free services for the public.
NET.mission: To give businesses everywhere cloud-based security, faster websites, and building blocks for their own software.

NFLX.short: Netflix — the world's largest video streaming service.
NFLX.operations: Streams series, films, games and live programmes in many languages to paying subscribers who watch on televisions, phones and set-top boxes around the world.
NFLX.mission: To be a worldwide entertainment service offering a wide range of programmes people can watch whenever they choose.

NNE.short: Early-stage developer of very small ('micro') nuclear reactors.
NNE.operations: Early-stage firm designing four small reactors (KRONOS, LOKI, ZEUS, ODIN) and planning a uranium fuel processing plant plus fuel transport and consulting work.
NNE.mission: To build very small nuclear reactors for remote and specialised sites and to supply the fuel for them.

NOC.short: Builds the B-21 stealth bomber, nuclear missiles and space systems.
NOC.operations: Four segments - aircraft, defence, mission and space systems - with work in the United States, Asia-Pacific, Europe and other countries.
NOC.mission: To supply aircraft, nuclear deterrent systems, satellites and military command and communication systems to defence customers.

NOK.short: Nokia — telecom network equipment, now also selling data-centre networking.
NOK.operations: Supplies mobile, fixed-line and internet network equipment across the Americas, China, India, Asia Pacific, Europe, the Middle East and Africa through four business segments.
NOK.mission: To provide the mobile, fixed and cloud networks that carry communications, and to license its patents and brand.

NOW.short: ServiceNow — workflow software that automates company IT and HR tasks.
NOW.operations: Sells through resellers and partners in North America, Brazil, Europe, Africa, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific to government, banks, hospitals and manufacturers.
NOW.mission: To provide internet-based software that organises and automates the everyday work flowing between a company's departments.

NRG.short: Texas power producer and retail electricity seller, with a large data-centre deal.
NRG.operations: Sells electricity and home services to households and businesses in the US and Canada under names such as NRG, Reliant and Vivint, and owns power plants.
NRG.mission: To supply homes and businesses with electricity while helping them manage their energy use and protect their property.

NU.short: Nu Holdings — Latin America's largest digital-only bank.
NU.operations: Runs a branchless digital bank serving customers in Brazil, Mexico, Colombia, the Cayman Islands and the United States.
NU.mission: To offer everyday banking, cards, loans, savings and insurance entirely through a mobile phone app.

NVDA.short: Makes the GPU chips that almost all AI computing runs on.
NVDA.operations: Sells computing and graphics chips through two arms, with operations in the United States, Taiwan, China, Hong Kong and Europe.
NVDA.mission: To operate as a company that supplies the computing equipment whole data centres use for artificial intelligence.

NVT.short: nVent — electrical enclosures and liquid cooling systems for data centres.
NVT.operations: Makes enclosures, cooling, cable management and electrical connection products under brands such as HOFFMAN and ERICO for data centres, industry and infrastructure worldwide.
NVT.mission: To connect and protect electrical systems in demanding settings such as data centres and industrial sites.

OKLO.short: Developing small fast reactors to power data centres; earned its first revenue in 2026.
OKLO.operations: Developing small nuclear plants called Aurora Powerhouse, each making 15 to 75 megawatts, plus technology to turn used nuclear fuel back into usable fuel.
OKLO.mission: To supply electricity at large scale to US customers from its own small nuclear power plants.

ON.short: Power and sensing chips for electric cars, industry and AI data centres.
ON.operations: Runs three product groups covering power, analogue and sensing chips, with operations in Hong Kong, Singapore, the United Kingdom and the United States.
ON.mission: To provide sensing and power-handling chips used in cars, factories and other industrial equipment.

ONDS.short: Defence and security drones and counter-drone systems, plus private wireless networks.
ONDS.operations: Two arms, private wireless networks and drones, sold in the US and abroad to railways, utilities, oil and gas firms, public safety bodies and government.
ONDS.mission: To provide secure private wireless communications and self-flying drones that gather data and defend against hostile drones.

ORCL.short: Databases and business software, and now a large AI cloud provider.
ORCL.operations: Sells worldwide, directly and through partners, to businesses, government agencies and schools, supplying computing equipment alongside its software.
ORCL.mission: To supply the databases, business software and rented computing power that organisations use to run their operations.

OUST.short: Lidar sensors — the 'eyes' for robots and self-driving vehicles.
OUST.operations: Makes laser-based distance sensors sold to car, industrial, robotics and infrastructure customers across the Americas, Asia, Europe, the Middle East and Africa.
OUST.mission: To supply sensors that let vehicles, robots and public infrastructure see and understand what is around them.

PANW.short: Palo Alto Networks — the largest pure-play cybersecurity company.
PANW.operations: Sells computer security products to companies, telecoms firms and governments across the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Asia Pacific and Japan.
PANW.mission: To protect customers' networks, cloud systems, security teams and their new artificial intelligence systems.

PL.short: Operates satellites that photograph the whole Earth daily and sells the imagery.
PL.operations: Designs, builds and launches its own fleets of satellites, then sells frequent pictures of the Earth through an online service worldwide.
PL.mission: To photograph the Earth often and sell that imagery to farming, mapping, energy, forestry, finance and government customers.

PLTR.short: Software that helps governments and companies make sense of huge amounts of data.
PLTR.operations: Sells software platforms in the United States, the United Kingdom and internationally, serving intelligence and defence agencies as well as businesses.
PLTR.mission: To build software that helps governments and companies make sense of large amounts of data, including through artificial intelligence.

POET.short: Small developer of optical 'engines' that combine light and electronics on one chip.
POET.operations: Small Toronto-based firm selling chip packaging and optical parts across the Americas, Europe and Asia, working with partner Lumilens.
POET.mission: Aims to combine electronic and light-based parts on a single chip for data centres and networks.

POWI.operations: Designs and makes high-voltage power conversion chips used in phones, appliances, TVs, LED lighting, electric vehicles, solar and wind systems and electric trains.
POWI.mission: To supply the chips that convert high-voltage electricity into the lower voltages equipment needs.

POWL.short: Powell — electrical switchgear for utilities, industry and data centres.
POWL.operations: Builds custom electrical switchgear and control-room modules for refineries, liquefied natural gas plants, utilities, data centres and mining, in the US, Canada, Middle East and Asia.
POWL.mission: To design, build and service the heavy electrical equipment industrial plants use to control power.

PWR.short: Quanta Services — builds and maintains electricity transmission lines.
PWR.operations: Two divisions build and service electric power lines and substations, and underground gas, oil and industrial infrastructure, for utilities and energy companies.
PWR.mission: To build and maintain the infrastructure that delivers electricity, gas and communications.

PYPL.short: PayPal — online payments and the Venmo app.
PYPL.operations: Runs an online payments network linking shops and shoppers worldwide, under names including PayPal, Venmo, Braintree, Xoom and Honey.
PYPL.mission: To let people and businesses anywhere pay, send and receive money digitally.

QCOM.short: Smartphone processors and modems, expanding into cars and AI laptops.
QCOM.operations: Runs three arms worldwide: chip products, patent licensing and start-up investing, plus government services and data-centre products.
QCOM.mission: To develop and commercialise the basic technologies that the wireless telephone industry depends on.

RBRK.short: Rubrik — data backup and fast recovery after ransomware attacks.
RBRK.operations: Sells data protection and backup services worldwide to customers in finance, retail, transport, energy, healthcare, education and the public sector.
RBRK.mission: To keep customers' data safe and help them recover quickly after a cyber attack.

RCAT.short: Small military drones; its Black Widow won a US Army reconnaissance programme.
RCAT.operations: Designs and makes small drones and uncrewed boats in the United States for defence, national security and commercial users such as police and inspectors.
RCAT.mission: To supply small unmanned aircraft and robotic systems used for reconnaissance, surveillance and defence missions.

RKLB.short: Small rockets and satellites — a leading commercial space launch company.
RKLB.operations: Provides rocket launches and builds spacecraft, serving customers in the United States, Canada, Japan and elsewhere through two business segments.
RKLB.mission: To launch small and medium rockets and supply satellites and parts for commercial and government space missions.

ROK.short: Factory automation equipment and industrial control software.
ROK.operations: Supplies factory automation equipment, software and servicing across North America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Asia Pacific and Latin America.
ROK.mission: To help manufacturers in industries such as cars, food and energy run their plants automatically and with modern digital tools.

RTX.short: Patriot and AIM-9X missiles, jet engines, and aerospace components.
RTX.operations: Three segments - Collins Aerospace, Pratt & Whitney aircraft engines and Raytheon - serving commercial, military and government customers worldwide.
RTX.mission: To provide aerospace and defence systems and services to commercial, military and government customers around the world.

SBUX.operations: Roasts and sells coffee through its own and licensed stores internationally, and sells packaged coffee via grocery and food-service accounts.
SBUX.mission: Aims to be a leading roaster, marketer and retailer of coffee worldwide, selling drinks, food and packaged coffee under brands such as Starbucks and Teavana.

SE.short: Sea Limited — Shopee shopping, Garena games and Monee payments across South-East Asia.
SE.operations: Runs the Shopee shopping marketplace, the Garena games business and Monee financial services across Southeast Asia and Latin America.
SE.mission: To bring shopping, games and financial services to people across Southeast Asia and other regions through one technology company.

SHOP.short: Shopify — the software that lets anyone set up and run an online store.
SHOP.operations: Provides software that lets shopkeepers of any size sell online, in physical stores and on marketplaces, and handles their payments, shipping and till equipment.
SHOP.mission: To give merchants of any size the tools to run a business and sell wherever their customers are.

SIDU.short: Very small company that 3D-prints compact satellites; still early stage.
SIDU.operations: Designs, builds and flies small satellites from its own plant in Merritt Island, Florida, which handles machining, 3D printing, assembly and testing.
SIDU.mission: To build and operate its own satellites and sell the data they gather to commercial, aerospace, government and defence customers.

SKHY.short: Korean memory maker — the leading supplier of HBM memory used by AI chips.
SKHY.operations: Korean maker of memory and storage chips selling across Korea, China, the rest of Asia, the United States and Europe; also makes chips to order.
SKHY.mission: Aims to supply memory and storage chips for servers, phones, computers and cars.

SMCI.short: Builds the AI server racks that house Nvidia's chips.
SMCI.operations: Designs and sells computer servers and storage systems in the United States, Asia and Europe, including complete racks installed in data centres.
SMCI.mission: To supply servers built on modular, open designs for data centre, cloud and artificial intelligence customers.

SMR.short: NuScale — designer of small modular nuclear reactors.
SMR.operations: Sells small modular reactor units of 77 megawatts each and the design, licensing, construction, training and maintenance support that plants using them need.
SMR.mission: To provide small modular nuclear reactor technology and the services required to license, build and run plants using it.

SNDK.short: Flash memory and SSD storage, spun out of Western Digital.
SNDK.operations: Makes flash-memory drives and cards, selling in the US, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia to computer makers, data centres and retailers.
SNDK.mission: Aims to supply fast flash storage for computers, phones, cars and data centres.

SNOW.short: Cloud data warehouse where companies store and analyse all their data.
SNOW.operations: Sells its internet-based data platform to organisations of many kinds in the United States and internationally.
SNOW.mission: To let organisations gather all their data in one place to gain business insight, share it, and apply artificial intelligence to it.

SOFI.short: SoFi — a digital bank combining loans, investing and banking in one app.
SOFI.operations: A lender and online bank serving the United States, Latin America, Canada and Hong Kong, split into lending, banking technology, and financial services.
SOFI.mission: To let its members borrow, save, spend, invest and protect their money in one place.

SOUN.short: SoundHound — voice AI for restaurant drive-thrus, cars and call centres.
SOUN.operations: Builds voice-recognition software used in cars, televisions, restaurant ordering and customer service, sold in the US, Japan, Korea, France and Germany.
SOUN.mission: To let people speak to machines in ordinary language and get useful answers back.

SPCX.short: SpaceX — rockets, Starship, and the Starlink satellite internet network.
SPCX.operations: Launches reusable rockets, runs the Starlink satellite internet network, and operates an artificial intelligence arm; serves the US, Ireland, Canada and beyond.
SPCX.mission: To provide low-cost access to space with reusable rockets, deliver internet from satellites, and build artificial intelligence services.

STRL.short: Does the site groundwork and utilities underneath data centres and chip plants.
STRL.operations: Prepares sites for data centres, warehouses and power plants, builds roads, bridges and airports, and pours house foundations across the southern and eastern United States.
STRL.mission: To provide site preparation, transport construction and building work in the United States through three business segments.

STX.short: Hard disk drives — the bulk storage that fills data centres.
STX.operations: Supplies storage drives and systems from Singapore, the United States and the Netherlands, selling to equipment makers, distributors and retailers.
STX.mission: Aims to provide the drives and systems that store the world's growing pile of data.

TE.short: Solar manufacturing company (formerly Freyr) building US solar capacity.
TE.operations: Makes and sells solar panels and cells, with a head office in Austin, Texas, a factory south of Dallas, and activity in Norway.
TE.mission: To build an American-based supply chain for solar panels and cells; it was the battery firm FREYR until renaming itself in February 2025.

TEAM.short: Atlassian — Jira, Confluence and Trello, the tools teams use to track work.
TEAM.operations: Sells worldwide a family of teamwork tools, including Jira for tracking projects, Confluence for shared documents and Trello for to-do lists.
TEAM.mission: To connect all the teams in an organisation through one shared system of work so they can get more done.

TEM.short: Tempus AI — applies AI to medical and genetic data to guide cancer treatment.
TEM.operations: Runs laboratories and a data service in the United States that test patients' genes for doctors, and works with drug makers such as AstraZeneca and Merck.
TEM.mission: Aims to link doctors directly to its own laboratory testing and large stores of patient data so treatment choices are better informed.

TER.short: Machines that test finished chips, plus industrial and collaborative robots.
TER.operations: Designs and sells machines that test computer chips, and also makes robots, operating in the United States, Asia Pacific, Europe, the Middle East and Africa.
TER.mission: To supply the testing equipment that checks chips work properly, plus robots that work alongside people in factories.

TMDX.short: 'Organ-in-a-box' machines that keep donor organs alive during transport.
TMDX.operations: Sells its Organ Care System, a portable machine that keeps donor organs alive outside the body, to transplant centres in the United States and abroad.
TMDX.mission: Aims to transform organ transplant treatment for patients whose organs have failed.

TSLA.short: Electric cars, plus a fast-growing battery-storage business and robotics ambitions.
TSLA.operations: Builds and sells electric cars plus energy generation and storage systems in the United States, China and other countries, across two business segments.
TSLA.mission: To sell electric vehicles alongside solar and battery storage products, with related services such as financing, servicing and insurance.

TSM.short: The world's chip factory — actually manufactures the chips Nvidia, Apple and AMD design.
TSM.operations: Makes, packages and tests chips for other companies, selling in Taiwan, China, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Japan and the United States.
TSM.mission: To manufacture the chips its customers design, for computing, phones, cars, connected devices and home electronics.

UBER.short: Uber — ride-hailing and food delivery around the world.
UBER.operations: Runs a phone app linking riders with drivers and hire cars, diners with restaurants and shops, and companies shipping goods with lorry drivers.
UBER.mission: To make getting a ride, a meal or a delivery as simple as pressing a button on a phone.

UNH.short: America's largest health insurer, plus a very large healthcare services arm.
UNH.operations: Sells health insurance to employers, governments and individuals, and through its Optum arm provides medical care, pharmacy services and health software.
UNH.mission: Aims to run a health care company that both provides insurance cover and delivers the care, pharmacy and data services behind it.

UUUU.short: US uranium miner that also processes rare-earth elements at its Utah mill.
UUUU.operations: Explores for and recovers uranium from mineral properties in the United States, and also produces vanadium, rare earth materials and heavy mineral sands such as zircon and ilmenite.
UUUU.mission: To find, recover and sell uranium and other critical minerals from its US mineral properties.

V.short: Visa — the world's largest payment network, earning a small fee on card transactions.
V.operations: Runs VisaNet, a network that approves and settles card payments in the United States and internationally for banks, shops and governments.
V.mission: To move money for consumers, sellers, banks and governments through its payment network and card brands.

VEEV.short: Cloud software built specifically for pharmaceutical and life-science companies.
VEEV.operations: Serves drug and medical companies in North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East, Africa and Latin America, adding consulting and support services.
VEEV.mission: To provide the online software and data that drug and medical firms use to run sales, clinical trials, quality checks and regulatory paperwork.

VRT.short: Vertiv — the power and cooling systems that keep data centres running.
VRT.operations: Makes the power and cooling equipment that keeps data centres and telephone networks running in more than 40 countries, under brands such as Liebert.
VRT.mission: To keep the equipment behind data centres and networks powered, cooled and running without interruption.

VST.short: Vistra — Texas power producer with nuclear and gas plants serving AI demand.
VST.operations: Serves about 5 million electricity and gas customers and runs roughly 44,000 megawatts of gas, nuclear, coal, solar and battery generation across US states.
VST.mission: To generate electricity and sell it, along with natural gas, directly to homes, businesses and industry across the United States.

WDAY.short: Workday — cloud software for company HR and finance departments.
WDAY.operations: Sells internet-based software that large employers use to run pay, hiring and accounting, serving banks, hospitals, schools, governments, shops and manufacturers.
WDAY.mission: To give organisations one online system for managing their people and their money.

WDC.short: Hard drives and storage systems for data centres and consumers.
WDC.operations: Makes hard-disk drives and storage systems sold across the US, Asia, Europe, the Middle East and Africa through computer makers, dealers and retailers.
WDC.mission: Aims to supply large-capacity hard drives for homes, offices and data centres.

XE.short: X-energy — small modular reactor developer; listed on the market in April 2026.
XE.operations: Designs nuclear reactors and makes their fuel; its Xe-100 unit produces 80 megawatts of electricity or 200 megawatts of heat, and it manufactures TRISO-X reactor fuel.
XE.mission: To design and supply nuclear reactors together with the special fuel they run on.

YUM.short: Owns KFC, Pizza Hut and Taco Bell.
YUM.operations: Runs and franchises fast-food restaurants in the United States, China and internationally through four divisions: KFC, Taco Bell, Pizza Hut and Habit Burger & Grill.
YUM.mission: Aims to develop, operate and franchise quick-service restaurant brands around the world.

ZETA.short: Marketing software that uses data and AI to target customers.
ZETA.operations: Sells cloud-based marketing and customer-data software to large companies in the United States and other countries.
ZETA.mission: Aims to help large companies find, grow and keep customers more cheaply and effectively than rival marketing tools.

ZS.short: Zscaler — cloud security that replaces traditional corporate firewalls.
ZS.operations: Runs cloud-based security services worldwide that inspect the internet traffic between staff and the applications and files they use.
ZS.mission: To protect companies by checking every connection through the cloud rather than trusting anyone inside the network.

NXPI.short: NXP — the chips that run cars, factory machines and connected devices.
NXPI.operations: Runs sites in more than 30 countries across the Americas, Asia-Pacific and Europe, selling through its own sales offices and independent distributors.
NXPI.mission: Aims to build complete solutions rather than just products, expanding what people, organisations and society can do.

CSCO.short: Cisco — the routers, switches and security kit that connect offices, carriers and AI data centres.
CSCO.operations: Sells worldwide to businesses, governments and telecom carriers through its own sales force plus resellers, integrators and distributors.
CSCO.mission: Its stated purpose is to power an inclusive future for all.

CIEN.short: Ciena — the laser equipment that pushes huge amounts of data down fibre-optic cables.
CIEN.operations: Serves more than 1,700 customers across the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific, backed by 4,500+ research staff and 2,400+ patents.
CIEN.mission: Aims to build adaptive networks that keep pace with exploding bandwidth demand and help customers thrive in the AI era.

MTSI.short: MACOM — high-speed chips for military radar and satellites, plus the optical chips inside AI data centres.
MTSI.operations: Runs design centres, sales offices and manufacturing across North America, Europe and Asia, serving more than 6,000 end customers.

VIAV.short: VIAVI — test gear that checks networks actually work, plus the colour-shifting ink that stops banknote forgery.
VIAV.operations: Sells across the Americas, Asia-Pacific and Europe to telecom, cloud, enterprise, emergency-services, military and aerospace customers.
VIAV.mission: Positions itself as a global leader in test, measurement and optical technologies for critical infrastructure.

TSEM.short: Tower Semiconductor is a contract chip manufacturer - a foundry - but unlike the giants chasing the smallest, fastest digital chips, Tower specialises in analog and specialty chips: parts that handle radio signals, electrical power, light and sensing. Its customers are other chip companies and system makers who design the chips and pay Tower to build them, for use in mobile phones, data-centre optical networking gear, cars, industrial equipment and medical devices.
TSEM.operations: Runs wafer fabrication plants in Israel, the United States, Japan and Italy, and in July 2026 announced a roughly 3 billion dollar capacity expansion in Japan with Japanese government (METI) support. Q2 2026 revenue mix: RF Infrastructure 25 percent, RF Mobile 23 percent, Power 17 percent, Sensors and Displays 15 percent, Discrete 11 percent, mixed-signal/CMOS and other 9 percent. Listed on NASDAQ since October 1994 and dual-listed in Tel Aviv.
TSEM.mission: To be the analog specialty foundry of choice, and in particular to become a leading supplier of silicon photonics for AI data centres - management has taken that business from a 180 million dollar annualised run rate in Q2 2025 to 680 million in Q2 2026, targets 1 billion annualised by Q4 2026, has 1.3 billion of signed silicon photonics contracts for 2027, and has raised its 2028 model to 3.6 billion of revenue which it describes as fully spoken for by customers.

GFS.short: GlobalFoundries is a contract chip manufacturer that builds semiconductors designed by other companies. It deliberately does not compete at the bleeding edge of miniaturisation; instead it makes the more mature, feature-rich chips that go into phones, cars, home appliances, industrial equipment and networking gear - power management chips, radio-frequency modems, microcontrollers and, increasingly, silicon photonics and quantum-related parts.
GFS.operations: Operates fabs in the United States, Germany and Singapore. Q2 2026 end-market mix: Smart Mobile Devices 36 percent, Automotive 19 percent, Home and Industrial IoT 18 percent, Communications Infrastructure and Data Center 16 percent, Technology Services 11 percent. Roughly 73 percent owned by Mubadala of Abu Dhabi. Awarded up to 1.5 billion dollars of US CHIPS Act funding plus more than 550 million from New York State, and in July 2026 a further 300 million silicon photonics award under which the US government took an approximately 1 percent equity stake, plus a 375 million quantum computing letter of intent.
GFS.mission: To be the essential partner for feature-rich, mature-node chips that the world actually runs on, expanding into silicon photonics and quantum while keeping manufacturing inside the United States, Europe and Singapore rather than concentrating it in Taiwan.

FORM.short: FormFactor makes probe cards - precision electrical test fixtures that touch a silicon wafer so each chip can be tested for defects before the wafer is cut apart and the chips are packaged. That saves chipmakers from spending money packaging chips that were never going to work. It also sells a smaller line of laboratory instruments: probe stations, analytical probes, and thermal and cryogenic test systems.
FORM.operations: Sells worldwide to memory makers, logic and foundry chipmakers and research laboratories. Q2 2026 revenue split: Probe Cards 209.7 million dollars (81 percent) and Systems 48.5 million (19 percent). Sold its Chinese operations in Suzhou and Shanghai in February 2024 for 25 million dollars, retaining a distribution partnership there.
FORM.mission: To be the test and measurement partner that lets chipmakers find bad chips as early and as cheaply as possible - now aimed squarely at the two hardest new test problems in AI hardware: high-bandwidth memory, which was about two thirds of its record DRAM revenue in Q2 2026, and co-packaged optics, which management expects to pass 20 million dollars of revenue in 2026.

COHU.short: Cohu makes the machines and parts used to test computer chips after they have been manufactured and packaged - mainly test handlers that move chips into and out of a tester at controlled temperatures, plus the contactors and probe pins that physically touch each chip, inspection and measurement systems, and software that analyses the test data.
COHU.operations: Operates across the Americas, Europe and Asia including the United States, Switzerland, Germany, Malaysia, the Philippines, Japan and Singapore. Sells to semiconductor makers and to the outsourced assembly and test houses that serve them, across automotive, computing, industrial, mobile, consumer and IoT applications. Recurring revenue - consumables and interface products rather than machines - was 53 percent of revenue in Q2 2026.
COHU.mission: To shift the business away from lumpy machine sales toward steady recurring revenue, and to ride the move from its traditional automotive base into AI compute - computing was 46 percent of system orders in Q2 2026, up 150 percent year on year, and management raised its 2026 high-performance-compute revenue estimate to 100-110 million dollars against an opportunity pipeline of roughly 850 million.
